#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
Update API functions in Lean to reflect web API changes. 

#### Related Issue
<!--- This project only accepts pull requests related to open issues -->
<!--- If suggesting a new feature or change, please discuss it in an issue first -->
<!--- If fixing a bug, there should be an issue describing it with steps to reproduce -->
<!--- Please link to the issue here: -->
Closes #4983

#### Motivation and Context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
We need both the Web API and Lean API functions to be in sync for all functionality to be maintained.

#### Requires Documentation Change
<!--- Please indicate if these changes will require updates to documentation, and if so, specify what changes are required -->

There is a functional change in the behavior of the resulting `Backtest` object.

Now instead of having a `Result` obj as a member of `Backtest` (Backtest.Result) there is no longer a result object. Instead the members originally contained in the Result obj are now included in the `Backtest` obj. 

So before where you would use `Backtest.Result.Charts` you will just use `Backtest.Charts`

pr_comments:
One error still persists in my tests but it is completely independent of lean and only springs up in special cases.

It is the SortinoRatio being sent by the web api in exponential format that breaks my de-serializing.
```{"Input string '7.9228162514264338e+28' is not a valid decimal. Path 'backtest.alphaRuntimeStatistics.SortinoRatio', line 1, position 16196."}```

Again this only occurs when the SortinoRatio is a very large value. It can be fixed at the endpoint as it has before.

**Edit:** Issue has been fixed with decimal converter

I initially implemented a custom de-serializer for AlphaRuntimeStatistics, and it worked, but it seemed to be too much for the issue and only addressed the SortinoRatio being a broken value and not any other decimals which could also break if it was in exponent format.

So, I thought I would scrap the initial custom de-serializer and create a small one specifically for decimals.

Now I am using the custom decimal converter I created which allows exponential notation for decimals via `decimal.Parse()` w/ `NumberStyles.float` as the style.


EDIT:
After rebasing onto master I found that just recently another JSON decimal converter was merged into master. I opted to use this because it was already in use and serves to implement the same functionality.

review_comments: Do we **need** this wrapper? Looks fishy, incompatibility between Lean and cloud api

With the new response structure it is, we could remove the success and error members from the backtest class though and not assign them like it is now. I wanted to keep those members though for users to know what could've gone wrong in their api call, because I stuck with returning just the backtest obj instead of returning the wrapped obj in the new class that contains those details
Just checking: there are some properties that the `BacktestResult` has that are now not present, should we add them? like for example `Orders/OrderEvents/ProfitLoss/RollingWindow/...`

Order/OrderEvents is not in the Backtest response so we don't have to worry about that one.

I went ahead and added RollingWindow and TotalPerformance so those are good to go.

ProfitLoss is having some issues because of a strange inconsistency in the web api. If there is no entries in the profitloss object the web api send a empty list, if there is, it sends a dictionary type (which is expected). Newtonsoft isn't happy about the empty list though when it expects a dictionary and fails to de-serialize.
Why not directly update the `result.Backtest.Charts` above instead of having the intermediate `updatedCharts`?
Changing the collection during enumeration threw a InvalidOperationException.r
